sentences.text: Koumpiodontosuchus was an extinct neosuchian crocodyliform that lived in the Early Cretaceous Wessex Formation of England. It is classified within the family Bernissartiidae.
Megan Jacobs discovered an isolated tooth that was twice the size of the holotype teeth.
The first fossilized skull fragment was discovered by Diane Trevarthen on a beach near Sandown on the Isle of Wight in March 2011.
A second skull fragment was found by Austin and Finley Nathan three months after the first discovery.
Paleontologist Steve Sweetman initially identified the fragments as belonging to Bernissartia fagesii due to their small size and button-shaped teeth.
Sweetman and colleagues named and described the new species in a 2015 paper published in Acta Palaeontologica Polonica.
Koumpiodontosuchus lived during the Barremian stage, between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago.
